paragraphs.title: The Prophet's Warning and the Locust Swarm

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that the word of the LORD came to Joel the son of Pethuel.
easy.q: To whom did the word of the LORD come?

answers: The old men and all the inhabitants of the land
easy.explanation: Joel addressed the old men and all the inhabitants of the land.
easy.q: Who was told to hear and give ear?

easy.explanation: The insects successively ate what remained of the crops.
easy.q: What did the locusts and other insects consume?

medium.explanation: They were told to tell their children, grandchildren, and another generation.
medium.q: What were the people commanded to do with this event?

answers: The crops were consumed in successive waves
Only one kind of plant was eaten
medium.explanation: Each insect ate what the previous insect had left.
medium.q: What does the sequence of insects in verse 4 show?

medium.explanation: The word refers to what remained after the earlier insect had eaten.
medium.q: What does the word “left” mean in the phrase “that which the palmerworm hath left”?

answers: The calamity affected the whole people and needed to be remembered
Only the old men had seen the locusts
Children were forbidden to hear about it
challenge.explanation: The broad address and command to tell future generations show that the event concerned everyone.
challenge.q: Why did Joel address both the old men and all the inhabitants of the land?

answers: The event was severe and unusual
The event happened only in the distant past
challenge.explanation: The question emphasizes that the calamity was extraordinary.
challenge.q: What does the question “Hath this been in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?” suggest?

answers: The first verses call the people to remember and tell, while verse 4 describes the reason
The first verses concern the temple, while verse 4 concerns the priests
The first verses describe rain, while verse 4 describes a harvest
challenge.explanation: The unusual destruction described in verse 4 is the event that must be remembered and reported.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between verses 2–3 and verse 4?

short_answers.question: Who was Joel's father?
short_answers.explanation: Joel is called the son of Pethuel in verse 1.

short_answers.question: Name one group told to hear Joel's message.
short_answers.answer: The old men, or the inhabitants of the land.

short_answers.question: What did the caterpiller eat?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 describes the insects eating in succession.

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of the Crops and the People's Mourning

easy.explanation: The verse addresses drunkards and all drinkers of wine.
easy.q: To whom was the command “Awake, ye drunkards, and weep” given?

answers: The pomegranate, palm, and apple trees
The olive, cedar, and fir trees
The almond, vine, and fig trees only
easy.explanation: Verse 12 names the vine, fig, pomegranate, palm, apple, and all the trees of the field.
easy.q: Which fruit trees are named in verse 12?

easy.explanation: The husbandmen and vinedressers were told to be ashamed and howl.
easy.q: Who was told to mourn over the loss of the harvest?

answers: The wine and fruit were harmed
The temple was filled with grain
medium.explanation: The damaged vines and fruit trees meant the loss of wine and fruit.
medium.q: What was the result of the destruction of the vine and fig tree?

medium.explanation: New wine is the produce of the grape harvest.
medium.q: What does “new wine” refer to in this passage?

answers: The field harvest and agricultural produce had perished
They were forbidden to enter the city
The temple vessels had been taken
medium.explanation: The wheat, barley, vines, and fruit trees had been destroyed.
medium.q: Why were the husbandmen and vinedressers called to mourn?

answers: The crops provided food and drink, so their destruction removed human joy
Joy disappeared because the temple was destroyed
There was no connection between crops and joy
challenge.explanation: Verse 12 says that joy was withered away from the sons of men as the trees withered.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the loss of crops and the loss of joy?

answers: It emphasizes the insects' destructive power
It shows that the insects were small and weak
It explains that they came from the sea
challenge.explanation: The lion imagery portrays the insects as powerful and destructive.
challenge.q: Why does describing the locust nation as having the teeth of a lion strengthen the picture of calamity?

answers: The devastation expands from wine and vines to the whole harvest and the trees
The passage moves from drought to rain
The passage moves from temple worship to building storehouses
challenge.explanation: The description broadens from wine and vines to grain, fruit trees, and human joy.

short_answers.question: What were the drinkers told to do?
short_answers.explanation: Joel called them to mourn because the new wine was cut off.

short_answers.question: What happened to the fig tree?
short_answers.answer: It was made clean bare and its branches were made white.
short_answers.explanation: Joel describes the severe stripping of the fig tree.

short_answers.question: What happened to joy?
short_answers.answer: It was withered away from the sons of men.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 12 connects the ruined trees with the loss of joy.

paragraphs.title: The Suspension of Temple Worship and the Call to Fast

easy.explanation: The priests were told to gird themselves with sackcloth.
easy.q: What were the priests commanded to wear?

answers: The meat offering and the drink offering
easy.explanation: The offerings were no longer available because of the crop failure.
easy.q: What was cut off from the house of the LORD?

answers: Gather, fast, and cry unto the LORD
easy.explanation: They were told to sanctify a fast, call an assembly, gather, and cry to the LORD.
easy.q: What was the people commanded to do?

answers: The meat offering and drink offering were cut off
medium.explanation: The passage directly connects their mourning with the loss of the offerings.

answers: Call for a wall to be built
Call the people to leave the land
medium.explanation: The command was to assemble the community before the LORD.
medium.q: What does “call a solemn assembly” mean?

answers: Both express communal repentance and appeal to God during calamity
The fast was meant to celebrate the harvest
The crying announced the beginning of fieldwork
medium.explanation: The people were to gather and fast as they cried to the LORD.
medium.q: What is the relationship between fasting and crying unto the LORD?

answers: The shortage affected worship as well as agricultural life
challenge.explanation: Without produce, the offerings could not be brought to the house of the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the loss of the offerings reveal about the severity of the crop destruction?

answers: A public response from the whole community was needed
Only elders were allowed to fast
The priests were not part of the people
challenge.explanation: The command includes the elders and all the inhabitants.
challenge.q: Why were both the elders and all the inhabitants of the land summoned?

answers: Mourning in sackcloth, sanctifying a fast, gathering, and crying to the LORD
Offering grain, distributing crops, and drinking wine
challenge.explanation: The verses move from priestly mourning to a public fast, assembly, and prayer.
challenge.q: What order of actions appears in these verses?

short_answers.question: What were the priests told to do in sackcloth?
short_answers.answer: Come and lie all night in sackcloth.
short_answers.explanation: The ministers of the altar were commanded to mourn in this way.

short_answers.question: Where were the people to gather?
short_answers.answer: Into the house of the LORD their God.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 14 commands the assembly to gather there.

short_answers.question: What were the people to cry unto?
short_answers.explanation: The final command of verse 14 is to cry unto the LORD.

paragraphs.title: The Day of the Lord and Scarcity in the Land

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that the day of the LORD is at hand.
easy.q: What is near according to verse 15?

easy.explanation: Verse 16 asks whether the meat was not cut off before their eyes.
easy.q: What was cut off before the people's eyes?

answers: They had lost the way to the temple
easy.explanation: The herds were perplexed because they had no pasture.

medium.explanation: The garners were laid desolate and the barns were broken down.
medium.q: What was laid desolate or broken down because of the shortage?

medium.explanation: Garners are places where grain and produce are stored.

answers: They could not reach the temple
medium.explanation: Pasture was necessary food for the cattle and sheep.
medium.q: Why did the beasts suffer when there was no pasture?

answers: It moves from food and joy to storehouses, fields, and animals
It moves from priests to the building of cities
It moves from wine to falling rain
challenge.explanation: The passage describes loss of food, joy, grain, storage places, and animal pasture.
challenge.q: How does the description of scarcity expand in verses 15–18?

answers: The scarcity and destruction are presented as signs of approaching judgment
The day of the LORD is presented as a successful harvest day
There is no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The warning about the day of the LORD introduces the description of destruction and want.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the day of the LORD and the described devastation?

answers: The distress affected different kinds of animals
challenge.explanation: Both herds and flocks were desolate because the land lacked pasture.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the mention of both cattle and sheep?

short_answers.question: How is the day of the LORD described?
short_answers.answer: It is at hand and will come as a destruction from the Almighty.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 15 describes its nearness and destructive character.

short_answers.question: What happened to the seed under the clods?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 17 says the seed was rotten under the clods.

short_answers.question: What happened to the corn?
short_answers.explanation: The corn was withered, contributing to the scarcity.

paragraphs.title: A Cry to the Lord in a Ravaged Land

easy.explanation: Joel says, “O LORD, to thee will I cry.”

answers: The pastures of the wilderness and the trees of the field
easy.explanation: The fire devoured the wilderness pastures and the flame burned the field trees.

answers: The rivers of waters were dried up
easy.explanation: The animals suffered because the water channels had dried up.
easy.q: Why did the beasts of the field cry unto the LORD?

medium.explanation: Joel describes fire devouring the pastures and burning the trees.
medium.q: What image is used for the spreading calamity?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to channels through which water flows.

answers: The insects destroy vegetation while dryness removes water from the animals
Drought causes the locusts to disappear
medium.explanation: The passage combines destruction of vegetation with dried-up water sources.
medium.q: How does drought add to the locust plague?

answers: Both express the suffering of a ravaged land and a plea to the LORD
The beasts were commanded to call a fast
Joel cried because the beasts destroyed the crops
challenge.explanation: Joel cries to the LORD, and the beasts also cry because they suffer from the drought and fire.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Joel's cry and the distress of the beasts?

answers: The land suffers both destructive heat and lack of water
The calamity is limited to vineyards
challenge.explanation: The two images present different aspects of the land's devastation.
challenge.q: What does the use of fire together with dried-up waters emphasize?

answers: The calamity affects animals as well as people
The beasts do not need water
challenge.explanation: The closing verses show that the whole land and its creatures are affected.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning the beasts of the field at the end of the chapter?

short_answers.question: What did Joel say he would do?
short_answers.explanation: Joel directly addressed the LORD in his distress.

short_answers.question: What did the flame burn?
short_answers.answer: All the trees of the field.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 19 says that the flame burned the trees of the field.

short_answers.question: What happened to the rivers of waters?
short_answers.explanation: Their drying caused the beasts of the field to cry.
